items.title: native — `source.attach(watching(source))`: the RECEIVER is borrowed while the ARGUMENT moves it (rustc E0505); reactive-42 wrote the node subscription as two statements to dodge it; the emitter should evaluate such an argument first (native-42's rule for a `&mut` argument whose place a later argument reads, applied to a by-value argument that moves the receiver's place)
items.body: Pin: the one-statement form builds and matches node. Sizing S.

items.title: `combine((a, b)).map(\|pair\| { let (x, y) = pair; x + y })` leaves `map`'s `U` OPEN: a destructuring `let` inside the closure does not carry the tuple's element types into the body's tail; annotating `pair` fixes it — under the flip `map` is a blanket, so this is the everyday spelling
items.discussion: reactive-42 (2026-09-25); repro in `sweeps/order42/reactive-42/finds/`; B392's family (a closure typed from its body)
items.body: Fix: a destructuring `let` of a closure parameter binds the pattern's names from the parameter's inferred tuple type before the tail is typed. Pin red-first. Sizing S; solver.

items.title: over an IN-PROCESS transport, `sub`/`effect` on a node over a MIRROR sees the inline SEED twice (over a socket it is correct): the mirror's seed arrives inline under the subscribing turn and the node's pull re-reads it — a std design question (the in-process transport's inline delivery vs the push-pull protocol's one-notify-per-settle)
items.body: Options: (a) the in-process transport delivers the seed through the draining turn like a socket does (one code path — rec); (b) the node dedups a notify whose value equals its last pull (costs `PartialEq`); (c) document it. Rec (a). Sizing S–M; std/reactive, Order 43.

items.title: the regime-3 `;` steer (a missing return value) is not reached through `.map(..).cell()`: the expectation stops at the receiver, so a `;`-ended closure body inside `map` followed by `.cell()` gets the plain mismatch instead of the steer; B421 (the `dyn` coercion accepting a void body — a MISCOMPILE) is the same blind spot at a coercion
items.discussion: reactive-42 (2026-09-25); B421; the regime-3 pin re-anchored on a `Map<SignalCell<i32>, i32, i32>` annotation meanwhile
items.body: Fix: the expected-type walk carries the steer through a method chain whose receiver is a closure-taking call. Sizing S.
